title: feat(core): multi-resolution volume textures, the base for task T2
abstract:
﻿## What this pull request does

A volume of many images does not always fit in one GPU texture. A series of 2464 images
exceeds the limit of 2048 voxels on one axis that every known device states. Before this
work, the allocation of that texture failed, and the viewer showed nothing.

This work gives a volume more than one representation of its voxels. One representation
holds the data that the loader delivered. Another holds a box average of that data on a
coarser grid. A viewport chooses the representation that its device can hold, and it draws
that representation.

This branch is the base of task T2 of
[#2921](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/issues/2921). @mbellehumeur will
merge his later steps into this branch as he completes them.

## The three parts of this pull request

> Edited on 2026-11-04. Two pull requests that were based on this branch are now squashed into
> it, so that one pull request holds the whole set. Each part keeps its own commit, so a reviewer
> can read each part alone.

| Part | What it does | Where it is | Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Multi-resolution volume textures | The representations of a volume, the reduced textures, the GPU settings presets, and the flags of lossy downsampling | The commits of this branch up to the merge of `main`, [`abc361e2e`](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/commit/abc361e2e4ad52e26ae7ea1bab24f778c92a762f) | 132 files, +20730 −420 |
| 2. The viewport fidelity state, event and indicator | The fidelity state of a viewport, the `VIEWPORT_FIDELITY_CHANGED` event, and the indicator on the canvas | One squash commit, [`3ea2420b9`](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/commit/3ea2420b9e98c0fb5c9c0b9f4338bfb46d19e50f), from #2992 by @mbellehumeur | 62 files, +6004 −104 |
| 3. The acquired frames in the acquisition plane | A `PLANAR_NEXT` viewport draws the original frames in the acquisition plane of a reduced volume | One squash commit, [`e99bd737b`](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/commit/e99bd737b0c370e96b47253d9598ea94cc6cce9e), from #3018 | 19 files, +1367 −61 |

Closes #3017

### How to review each part

Review the parts in the order of the table. Part 2 uses part 1, and part 3 uses parts 1 and 2.

**Part 1.** Follow the section "How to review this pull request" below. To see only this part:

```sh

```

```sh
git show 3ea2420b9
```

1. `packages/docs/docs/specs/core/viewport-fidelity.md`: the requirements of the fidelity state.
2. `packages/core/src/RenderingEngine/helpers/fidelityIndicator/`: the state, the

4. The tests under `packages/core/test/` that name the fidelity.

The indicator attaches to each viewport, unless the application sets
`dangerouslyDisableFidelityIndicator`.

**Part 3.** The discussion is in #3018, and the requirements are AQP-U-1 to AQP-U-3 and
AQP-I-1 to AQP-I-10 of #3017.

4. `packages/core/src/RenderingEngine/GenericViewport/Planar/VtkVolumeSliceRenderPath.ts` and

5. `packages/core/test/planarAcquiredFrames.jest.js`, and the block `vtkVolumeSliceFrames` in

On the head before the squash of part 3 (the same tree), `npx jest` gave 198 suites: 2948 tests

In the full browser suite, 18 tests in 5 other files also fail without these changes.

#3022 (the GPU settings preset `auto`) is a draft that now targets this branch. It is not part of
this review.

## How to review this pull request

### Read the design first

Three pages hold the design. Read them before the code, in this order:

1. [Volume Render Strategy](https://pr-2931--cornerstone-3d-docs.netlify.app/docs/concepts/cornerstone-core/volumeRenderStrategy/)
   gives the pieces, the contracts (`VRS-C-*`) and the implementation choices (`VRS-I-*`).
   Its section "Where the code is" gives the file of each piece.
2. [Volume Render Sequences](https://pr-2931--cornerstone-3d-docs.netlify.app/docs/concepts/cornerstone-core/volumeRenderSequences/)
   gives six sequence diagrams with the real function names:
   - the GPU settings preset and the creation of the volume
   - the choice of the texture when a viewport adds its actor
   - the delivery of the images
   - the fill of a reduced texture in a render
   - the selection of a strategy on each render
   - a segmentation over a reduced volume
3. [Composite Voxel Manager](https://pr-2931--cornerstone-3d-docs.netlify.app/docs/concepts/cornerstone-core/compositeVoxelManager/)
   gives the model of the representations, the selection rule, and the arithmetic.

The three links go to the docs preview of this pull request. The pages are in the docs
build, under Concepts > Core. The docs site draws the Mermaid diagrams.

`resolveVolumeTexture` is the one place that a legacy viewport and a viewport of the
generic architecture share. `defaultVolumeStrategyProvider` calls
`boxAverageReductionFactors` with the limits of the active GPU settings preset, when final
downsampling is on. When every factor is 1,
the viewport gets the set `full-resolution/full-extent`, as before this pull request.
Otherwise the viewport gets a reduced set, for example `reduced-1x1x2/full-extent/average`.

### Then read the commits

The 14 commits are in a deliberate order, and each one builds and tests on its own. Read
them in order. The table gives the purpose of each commit, and the notes below the table
give the questions that matter most for each group.

| # | Commit | What it does |
| - | ------ | ------------ |
| 1 | `refactor(core): extract a real IVoxelManager interface from the class` | A pure refactor. It changes no behaviour. |
| 2 | `feat(core): add the grid descriptor and the box average arithmetic` | The `VoxelGrid` type, and the reduction of a grid by a box on each axis. |
| 3 | `feat(core): add the composite voxel manager` | The object that holds the representations, and that reads the best one. |
| 4 | `feat(core): add the quality record and the comparison function` | What a loader has delivered, and at which quality. |
| 5 | `feat(core): add the composite of the representations to ImageVolume` | The composite reaches a volume. |
| 6 | `feat(core): give a volume named sets of textures` | A global store of the textures, with a budget and an eviction rule. |
| 7 | `feat(core): choose a render strategy, and reduce a texture to fit the device` | The strategy, the GPU settings preset (a "capability profile" in that commit), and the MPR render path. |
| 8 | `feat(core): choose a strategy for the 3D render path and for a legacy viewport` | The same for the 3D path, and for the viewports of the existing architecture. |
| 9 | `fix(core): repair the 3D viewport of the generic path, and fill a reduced texture directly` | Three defects that a browser found in commit 8. |
| 10 | `chore(examples): take the CT of 2464 images from the public server` | Test data. |
| 11 | `feat(core): keep the true decoded size, and follow the load with a derivation` | The loader, and the update of a derived representation. |
| 12 | `fix(core): report rather than throw when a viewport holds no volume to scroll` | A defect that reaches a user as an exception. |
| 13 | `feat(examples): show a multi-resolution progressive load in the volume example` | The example that tests all of it. |
| 14 | `docs(core): describe how a derived representation follows the load` | The two design documents. |

### Commits 1 to 4: the model

These four commits add code, and no existing viewport calls that code. A reviewer can
read them as a library.

The question that matters: **is the model correct?** Four axes describe a representation,
and an earlier version of this design confused two of them. A region, a phase, an
arithmetic and a statistic are separate things. Many grids may exist at one resolution,
each one covering a different part of the volume.

### Commits 5 to 8: the render path

The question that matters: **does an existing viewport still behave as it did?** A volume
that fits in one texture takes the same path as before. A reviewer must find the place
where the two paths separate, and must agree that a device which can hold the data still
gets the data.

Commit 6 changes three lines of `BaseStreamingImageVolume`, and commit 11 depends on
those three lines.

### Commit 11: the loader

This commit is the largest, and it holds four separate changes. A reviewer may want to
read it as four:

1. **The loader keeps the true decoded size.** The request states the type of the buffer
   and no size, so an image keeps the size that the decoder produced. Before this change
   a frame that decoded small was replicated up to the size of the volume before anything
   read it, and the saving disappeared. The voxel manager of the volume now scales such
   an image when it reads it, with the arithmetic that the loader used, so the primary
   grid gives the values that it gave before.
2. **A derived representation follows the load.** `createRepresentation` reduces the data
   that the composite holds at that moment, and a streaming loader delivers its frames
   after that moment. Each delivery now redoes the boxes that the frame touches, and only
   those boxes.
3. **Two performance defects.** `getSliceData` composed a slice voxel by voxel, which
   took about 45 seconds on a volume of 512 x 512 x 2464. The longest task is now about
   1.1 seconds.
4. **Two correctness defects, and both were visible to a user.** See the section below.

### The two defects that predate this branch

**A frame was marked before its image reached the cache.** The mark read nothing, and
nothing marked the frame again. 45 of 174 slices stayed empty, and a sagittal view showed
a black line for each one.

**A volume kept the voxel manager that it first resolved for a slice.** A progressive
loader puts a replicate of a nearby frame in the cache under the image id of this frame,
and the image of the frame itself arrives later. The volume kept the replicate for ever,
so the slice showed the voxels of another slice. A sagittal view showed a block of one
frame repeated.

`git log -S` puts the second defect in
[#2748](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/pull/2748), so it is a defect of
`main` and not of this branch. A reviewer may want these two fixes on `main` before this
branch merges.

## Changes after the first review

Six commits answer the review of @sedghi and the tests of the branch in OHIF. Each one builds and tests on its own.

| Commit | Commit message | What it does |
| ------ | -------------- | ------------ |
| `9cb369c7b` | `refactor(core): probe WebGL2 only, and remove the WebGL1 fallback` | vtk.js does not render with WebGL1, so the probe asks for a WebGL2 context only. |
| `793d575c7` | `perf(core): limit the reduced texture fill of one render, and average only loaded frames` | A scroll render no longer fills every dirty reduced slice. |
| `323ba0688` | `fix(core): keep a stack prefetch out of a progressive volume load` | A stack prefetch no longer competes with the interleaved stages of a volume. |
| `c980f088b` | `fix(core): take in the images that the cache already holds when a volume load starts` | The frames that a stack viewport loaded before MPR no longer stay gray. |
| `e85899eaf` | `feat(core): load a large volume in 64 stages of every 64th image` | The load no longer sweeps the volume from one end to the other. |
| `18e84450d` | `fix(core): set the sample distance of a volume mapper from the texture grid, within the maximum samples` | A long series no longer gives a vtk.js warning on each render. |

### The fill of a reduced texture

- One render fills at most 16 reduced slices that hold data. The render also stops after 8 ms, but only after it fills one slice. `rendering.reducedTextureFill` sets the two limits. The texture then requests another render, and the next fill starts where the last fill stopped.
- A reduced slice reads only the frames that arrived. Before this change, a frame that had not arrived became a frame of zeros, and the average became too low. A replicate counts only when no frame of the box arrived.
- `fillPlaneByAverage` reads the target column from a table, and keeps one row of sums. An integer texture gets the rounded average. Before this change, the value was truncated.
- The docs relax the rule "never a decimation" for a display. An interactive display or a lossy display of high-resolution data can use a decimation. A display of lower-resolution data uses the box average. The derivations on the CPU keep the box average.

The render still calculates the box average on the main thread. Issue [#2966](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/issues/2966) proposes to move the reduction out of the render, and to pace the renders of a load.

### The stack prefetch

A stack viewport queues a cache fill of its whole series, from the top down, with up to 25 prefetch slots. A switch to MPR did not cancel that fill. The interleaved stages of the volume use 5 thumbnail slots, so the stack fill took most of the bandwidth.

- A volume that starts a progressive load removes the queued prefetch requests of other loaders for its images.
- `stackPrefetch` and `stackContextPrefetch` queue nothing for a stack whose images a volume loads progressively.
- `cache.getVolumeContainingImageId` skips a volume with no image ids. Before this change, the search stopped at that volume.

### The images that the cache already holds

A stack viewport can load images of the series before a switch to MPR. Before this change, the volume did not know those images until its own stage requested them. A nearby fill also skipped those frames, because the cache already held a better image. The frames stayed empty until a late stage, and they showed gray.

- When `load()` starts, the volume delivers each fully loaded cached image to itself.
- The deliveries run in batches of at most 8 ms, so a volume whose images are all cached does not stall. A cancelled or a restarted load stops the batches.
- A delivery only marks the texture slices. Each render fills them under the budget of `rendering.reducedTextureFill`.

### The 64 stages of a large volume

Before this change, the coarse configuration had three stages of every 64th image, and then the stock stages of every 4th image. Each stock stage retrieves its images in index order, so the load swept the volume from one end to the other.

- `coarseInterleavedRetrieveStages` now holds 64 stages of every 64th image.
- The offsets follow the bit-reversed order 0, 32, 16, 48, 8, 40, and so on. Each level of stages halves the gap between the retrieved images over the whole volume: 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1.
- Each image fills the frames up to half the gap of its level, and each image is retrieved once, at full resolution.
- `initialImages` retrieves the middle image and the last image. The last image closes the tail of a volume whose length is not a multiple of 64.
- This configuration has no lossy stage and no thumbnail stage. An HTJ2K server therefore gets no fast lossy first pass from it.

### The sample distance of a volume mapper

The sample distance was half the mean voxel side of the full-resolution volume. A series of 2464 images then needed about 5575 samples on its longest ray, which is more than the 4000 of `maximumSamplesPerRay`. vtk.js does not enforce that maximum. It wrote a warning on each render, and it sampled the whole ray.

- `sampleDistanceOf` uses half the mean voxel side of the grid that the texture holds. A reduced texture has a larger spacing, and a finer sample adds no detail.
- The distance never falls below the diagonal of the volume divided by 4000, so one ray needs no more than 4000 samples.
- The 3D render path sets the distance again when it binds a texture of another grid.

### GPU settings presets, and the flags of lossy downsampling

Two commits answer a discussion with the maintainers. Each one builds and tests on its own.

| Commit | Commit message | What it does |
| ------ | -------------- | ------------ |
| `cceb2eb19` | `feat(core): name the GPU settings presets, and turn on each lossy downsampling with an init flag` | The rename, the init flags, and the example parameter. |
| `a02709f99` | `docs(core): restore the code spans of the lossy downsampling notes` | A repair of the formatting of the docs of `cceb2eb19`. |

**The rename.** A "GPU capability profile" is now a "GPU settings preset". A preset is a named set of GPU settings: the largest texture edge, the texture memory and the speed. A preset does not describe a real device. The preset `auto` of #3022 computes the same values for the device.

| Before | After |
| ------ | ----- |
| `gpuCapabilityProfiles.ts` | `gpuSettingsPresets.ts` |
| `GpuCapabilityProfile` | `GpuSettings` |
| `GpuCapabilityProfileId` | `GpuSettingsPresetId` |
| `getGpuCapabilityProfile`, `getGpuCapabilityProfiles` | `getGpuSettingsPreset`, `getGpuSettingsPresets` |
| `getActiveGpuCapabilityProfile` | `getActiveGpuSettings` |
| `setActiveGpuCapabilityProfile`, `resetActiveGpuCapabilityProfile` | `setGpuSettingsPreset`, `resetGpuSettingsPreset` |
| `gridLimitsOfProfile` | `gridLimitsOfGpuSettings` |

The preset names do not change: `low-tablet`, `low`, `medium`, `high` and `high-texture-4096`.

**The flags.** The new init option `rendering.lossyDownsampling` turns on each kind of lossy downsampling:

| Flag | Default | What the flag turns on |
| ---- | ------- | ---------------------- |
| `final` | off | The reduced texture of a volume that does not fit the GPU settings. With `final` off, a viewport uploads the full-resolution texture, as before this pull request. |
| `interactive` | on | A larger sample distance during a rotation (`rotateSampleDistanceFactor` of `TrackballRotateTool` and `VolumeCroppingTool`), and the deferred resample of the CPU slice path. |
| `interleavedLoading` | on | The fill of a frame that has not arrived with a replicate of a nearby frame, in the interleaved stages of a progressive load. The default can change to off later. |

- `getLossyDownsampling()` and `setLossyDownsampling(change)` read and change the flags after the init.
- The examples read the URL parameter `?finalDownsampling=true|false` in `initDemo`. Only `volumeProgressive` turns final downsampling on. Its button "Reload with final downsampling off" reloads the example with the opposite value.
- The unit tests of the strategies turn final downsampling on. A new test checks the full-resolution texture with final downsampling off.

A change of behaviour: with the default flags, a volume that exceeds the GPU settings uploads at full resolution. A volume of 2464 images then fails to allocate on a device with an edge of 2048, as before this pull request. An application must turn on `final` to get the reduction.

### Changes to behaviour and to the API

- A browser that has WebGL1 and no WebGL2 now uses CPU rendering.
- `RenderingCapabilities.webgl2` is removed. `webgl` now states that a WebGL2 context exists.
- `canUseFloatOpacityTexture(context)` takes the context only.
- A progressive request now carries the `volumeId`, so `cancelLoading()` also removes the queued progressive requests.
- New: `ImageVolume.getImageQuality(imageIdIndex)`, `BaseStreamingImageVolume.isLoadingProgressively()`, and `rendering.reducedTextureFill` in the configuration.
- `coarseInterleavedRetrieveStages` changes from 3 coarse stages and the stock stages to 64 stages of every 64th image.
- The 3D and slab renders of a very long series, or of a reduced texture, use a larger sample distance.
- New: `sampleDistanceOf` and `MAXIMUM_SAMPLES_PER_RAY` in `createVolumeMapper`.
- The GPU capability profiles are now GPU settings presets. The table above gives the new names.
- New: `rendering.lossyDownsampling`, `getLossyDownsampling()` and `setLossyDownsampling()`. Final downsampling is off by default.

1883 unit tests pass in `packages/core` and `packages/tools`. The type check of `packages/core` and `packages/tools` reports no error. Nobody has measured the scroll, or checked the absence of the vtk.js warning, in a browser after these changes.

## Evidence

The measurements come from the example of commit 13, on a CT series of 2464 images of
512 x 512.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| ----------- | ------ | ----- |
| The longest single task of a load | 45 to 49 s | 1.1 s |
| The slices of a JLS thumbnail load that stayed empty | 45 of 174 | 0 |
| The voxels that differ between a linear load and a progressive load | 1446 of 2000 | 5 to 9 of 2000 |
| The size of a JLS thumbnail image in the cache | 512 x 512 | 128 x 128 |

1501 unit tests pass in `packages/core` and `packages/tools`. The type check of
`packages/core` reports no error.

## What this branch does not do

**The resolution of a viewport does not change while a volume loads.** The device sets
the resolution when the viewport adds its actor, and one resolution serves the whole
load. The values refine as the data arrives, so a reformat gets sharper, but the grid
does not get finer. A ladder of grids is later work.

**Nothing probes the device.** A GPU settings preset is a stated value and not a
measurement. #3022 adds the preset `auto`, which probes the device.

**The reduction of a texture slice still runs inside the render.** A limit for each render
bounds the work. Issue [#2966](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/issues/2966)
describes the later work.

**A residual difference of about 1% remains** between a linear load and a progressive
load. The volume agrees with its own cache exactly, so the difference is in what the
loader leaves in the cache. It produces no block and no line.

## Changes after the review of 2026-11-09

Twenty commits, `ffcb46072..44373daed`, answer the review. Each commit builds and tests on its
own. At `44373daed`, `tsc` gives no errors for `packages/core`. In `packages/core`, 84 jest suites
pass: 1201 tests pass, and 2 tests are skipped. Nobody ran these changes in a browser.

**Removed.** `08e1f1ff5` removes the reduced-copy pipeline, because no production code calls it.
The pipeline has 2614 lines of source, tests and docs. The branch `brick-loader` keeps the pipeline (see "Follow-up work").

**Changes of user requirements** in `specs/core/viewport-fidelity.md`. The maintainer approved
each change:

- FIDELITY-STATE-2 (`ec0ff36d7`): missing data is not lossy while the load runs. After the load
  ends, missing data is lossy, and the label is "Low Fidelity".
- The cause of a frame that is still missing after the load is `missingFrames`, and the hover
  text is "Missing frame(s)" (`44373daed`).
- FIDELITY-STATE-9 (`627f412c7`): a reduced labelmap over a full-resolution acquired frame
  adds a `reduced` line.
- The built-in indicator stays on for each lossy item, and that includes the interactive sample
  distance. 4.x showed lossy data with no indicator, and the migration notes call that
  behaviour a safety defect. The built-in indicator is a backup (FIDELITY-UI-10). An application
  that needs localized text or accessibility builds its own indicator from
  `VIEWPORT_FIDELITY_CHANGED`.

## Follow-up work

This pull request does not close the issues below. The issues hold work that remains after
this pull request merges.

- [ ] [#2966](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/issues/2966): volume textures.
  - The volume reduces the slices outside the render.
  - A pacer for each volume decides when a load renders.
  - The render copies only the bricks that its view needs, and an update copy records what
    each texture holds.
  - A preload states its retrieve configuration.
- [ ] [#3015](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/issues/3015): a labelmap with
  edge projection (MIP) uploads a full-resolution texture and does not reduce.
- [ ] The branch [`brick-loader`](https://github.com/cornerstonejs/cornerstone3D/tree/brick-loader):
  the reduced-copy pipeline.
  - The review of 2026-11-09 found that no production code calls this pipeline.
  - The pipeline includes `createVoxelRepresentation`, `createRepresentation`, the derivation in
    batches, `reducedVolumeImages.ts`, `MutableVolumeTextureSlab` and the brick index of
    `VolumeTextureSet`.
  - Commit `08e1f1ff5` of this pull request removes the pipeline. The branch `brick-loader` keeps
    the pipeline at `ffcb46072` for further development.
  - The pull request that first calls the pipeline brings the pipeline back, with these known
    defects fixed:
    - `createRepresentation` rounds a float volume.
    - Two reduced images can get the same image id.
    - A streaming volume computes each box one time for each frame.
    - A second delivery at the same quality does not refresh the derived boxes.

## Testing this against OHIF

OHIF pull request [OHIF/Viewers#6295](https://github.com/OHIF/Viewers/pull/6295) runs an
integrated build against this branch. Its deploy preview is
<https://deploy-preview-6295--ohif-dev.netlify.app>.

The test notes are
[Testing the Multi-Resolution Volume Work](https://github.com/OHIF/Viewers/blob/feat/multires-voxel-manager-base/platform/docs/docs/development/multiresolution-testing.md).
The page gives the URL of each GPU settings preset on the deploy preview, the checks, and a console
check of the texture grid that each viewport draws. The `?debug=true` stats overlay of OHIF
does not show the reduction.

OHIF turns on final downsampling only in the developer builds: `config/dev.js`,
`config/netlify.js`, `config/e2e.js` and `config/customization.js`. `config/default.js` and the
deployment configs keep it off. The customization `cornerstone.gpuSettingsPreset` selects a
preset, and also turns on final downsampling.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Volume rendering can select full- or reduced-resolution data to fit GPU capabilities, with quality details in the stats overlay.
  * Added configurable voxel representations and reduction statistics, including average and foreground-majority options.
